THE US DRAFTS · STILL UNDER STUDY Two proposed rules DRAFT RULE 901(C) · DEEPFAKES A burden-shifting test The challenger must first show evidence enough to support a finding of AI fabrication; a bare allegation isn't enough. Then the party relying on the item must prove it is more likely than not authentic. DRAFT RULE 707 · MACHINE-GENERATED EVIDENCE Expert-level reliability AI-generated evidence offered without an expert must meet the same reliability standards as expert testimony. Neither is final. The committee deferred 901(c) and withdrew 707 for revision; any new rule is years away. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 03 / 08

Two dangers, not one 1 Fake evidence gets in. A fabricated video, voice note or photo is admitted and decides the case. 2 Real evidence gets doubted. The "liar's dividend": a party dismisses genuine evidence by simply crying "deepfake". A good rule must stop both: keep fakes out without letting every genuine recording be waved away. Adv. THE GAP A hash proves a file hasn't changed, not that it was real to begin with A deepfake hashed at creation passes the integrity test perfectly. Indian law has no specific rule on who must prove what once someone alleges fabrication. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 05 / 08

Building blocks already exist 1 A threshold test like draft Rule 901(c): a specific showing of fabrication shifts the burden of proving authenticity. 2 Provenance by design: the Feb 2026 IT Rules already require AI tools to embed identifying metadata. Courts can ask for it. 3 Native files and metadata on demand: the Trade Marks Registry's draft AI rules already allow this. Courts can do the same. 4 Trained forensic capacity: more notified Examiners of Electronic Evidence (IT Act, s. 79A). Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

TA K E AWAY Authenticity is the next big evidence fight. When even AI companies say their output can't be reliably detected, courts can't rely on looking at evidence. They need clear burdens, provenance and forensic capacity. Indian courts should get ahead of this before the first big deepfake trial. Adv.
